summary.headline: Advait Energy Transitions Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR228 crore and PAT 55% to INR19.96 crore; order book hit a record INR1,304 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR228 crore (up 18% YoY), EBITDA of INR28.78 crore (up 49%, margin 12.61%) and PAT of INR19.96 crore (up 55%, margin 8.36%). For FY26, revenue was INR714.52 crore (up 80%), EBITDA INR83.78 crore (margin 11.73% vs 12.87%) and PAT INR58.08 crore (up 75%). The order book reached INR1,304 crore (up 159%), 64% power transmission solutions and 36% new and renewable energy. Management guided to 40%-plus revenue growth in FY27 and a dividend of INR2 per share was recommended. Standalone figures were also read out, with FY26 standalone revenue of INR448 crore and PAT of INR46 crore.

segments.name: Power transmission solutions (PTS)
segments.commentary: Accounts for 64% of the INR1,304 crore order book; products include OPGW, ERS, stringing tools, conductors and transformers. Management targets around 40%-50% growth from PTS for the next five years after the capex cycle.

segments.name: New and renewable energy (NRE)
segments.commentary: Accounts for 36% of the order book and about 25%-27% of FY26 revenue per management. Commissioned 75 MW of Adani's solar project at Khavda and has about 67.5 MW under execution there, due Q1 FY27. BESS EPC revenue of INR43 crore (reported as Q4 revenue of INR46 crore) came via group company Advait Green Energy.

segments.name: BESS and electrolysers (manufacturing build-out)
segments.commentary: Dholera multi-integrated facility is expected to be operational in Phase 1 by Q4 FY27, with 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser Phase 1 capacity. Management guided INR100-200 crore BESS manufacturing business in FY27 as the plant starts only around September-October 2026.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 40%-plus in FY27, described as conservative by management; it said FY26 growth was about 80%.
FY27 order book targeted at INR1,600-1,650 crore by end of FY27 against an order pipeline of about INR2,000 crore.
Segment mix shifting by about 10 percentage points a year; FY27 targeted at roughly 65:35 (PTS:NRE).
Margin improvement of about 1 percentage point expected in FY27; electrolyser margins 5%-10% initially, rising to about 20% in the subsequent year.
FY27 total capex of INR300-350 crore, including about INR137 crore for PTS/IPP and INR75 crore for BESS and electrolyser subsidiaries; FY26 PTS capex about INR100 crore funded internally.
Fuel cell: technology transfer with AVL and TECO for a plant in Ahmedabad; manual plant in about 1.5 years, automatic in 2-3 years; management sees about 500 MW of fuel cell demand within 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Solar EPC physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year, per management, with QRs now in place for large tenders.
Dholera facility: Phase 1 expected operational by Q4 FY27, covering 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser capacity; BESS plant to be 5 GWh over time.
Electrolyser module range: 250 kW, 500 kW, 1 MW, 2.5 MW and 5 MW single-stack, designed for a 100 MW project.
NABL accreditation received for the existing OPGW, ERS and stringing tools manufacturing facility.
Management expects BESS plant utilisation of 80%-85% in about a year and a half from start.
demand_pricing: Order execution timelines are typically 6 to 18 months depending on business type.

Largest-ever stringing tools and capital tools order of INR22 crore in Q4; ERS supply for MNRE of INR70 crore; first Uttarakhand EPC order of INR33 crore; GETCO re-conductoring EPC order of about INR27 crore.
Management said cost inflation in metals, fuel and other inputs compressed industry margins; conductor and transformer contracts have price-escalation clauses, but OPGW contracts do not.
New ALMM rules for solar from June 1: management said bids already factor them in, the split of government versus private order flow is about 50:50 to 60:40, and it expects limited cell-price impact.
Management expects fuel cell demand to start in FY26 but deliveries from FY27-28; applications are data-centre backup, ferries and defence.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance of 40% growth conservative given the INR1,300 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a little conservative: FY26 growth was about 80% and it expects robust growth in FY27. Order pipeline is about INR2,000 crore, with an FY27-end order book target of INR1,600-1,650 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 BESS revenue INR46 crore if BOO projects will sell electricity?
qa_highlights.answer: The BOO projects were awarded to the group company Advait Green Energy and booked as EPC revenue (INR43 crore). Electricity revenue will sit in SPVs and be consolidated after COD, likely from FY end.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY27 capex of about INR300-350 crore in total and expects about 1 percentage point of margin improvement in FY27. Electrolyser margins are expected at 5%-10% initially and about 20% in the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass on commodity cost inflation to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Conductor and transformer contracts have pass-through clauses; OPGW contracts do not. Management said it has factored these into its bid numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why were four subsidiaries created, and who holds the other 20% of one of them?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries were set up for focused growth, bank facilities and future equity raises, with AGPL for electrolysers and solar EPC, the battery company for BESS and C&I, Akara for carbon and Aura for assets. The 20% holder was not answered on the call and was deferred to email.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund capex and what about dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding will use both equity and debt in a mix based on business composition, and equity dilution would happen only if it benefits shareholders. No quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company move to pure-play solar EPC and what is the solar EPC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to bid on large tenders including module-supply projects and win some orders this year. Physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow was about INR5.8 crore against PAT of INR58 crore in FY26; management attributed this to working capital build-up from the Q4 revenue surge and gave no timeline for conversion.
Debt-equity rose to 0.46x from 0.23x, and management said further capex will need a mix of equity dilution and debt; no quantum was disclosed.
Margin pressure from metal and fuel cost inflation and from the NRE mix shift; Q4 consolidated EBITDA margin of 12.61% compares with 11.73% for FY26 and 12.87% in FY25.
Electrolyser and fuel cell timelines depend on government policy and market opening; the Dholera facility is due Q4 FY27 and fuel cell deliveries from FY27-28.
Ownership structure of the 80% subsidiary (Advait Carbon) was not clarified on the call.

Some answers were inconsistent: management cited Q4 standalone PAT as rising from INR15 crore to INR10 crore, and the Dholera BESS plant start timeline (Q4 FY27 versus September-October 2026) was not fully reconciled.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term energy transition story and order book, but evasive on specifics such as subsidiary ownership, funding quantum and fuel cell revenue. Management called its own FY27 growth guidance conservative, while acknowledging margin pressure from input costs.
key_quotes: So this year we could achieve about 80% revenue growth, and we are expecting robust growth for this year.
Physical capacity is close to 100 to 200 megawatt a year.
Our margins with our manufacturing facility being opened up for this year and having the sustained program for putting more manufacturing will keep on improved marginally.
So, cash flow is largely INR5.82 crores, which is you have mentioned correctly.
